verdict.rationale: Unstructured documents two relevant features: table-to-HTML enrichment, which outputs detected tables as HTML markup rather than typed rows, and a structured data extractor that writes values into a user-defined JSON schema. Together they partly deliver database-loadable output, but the docs never show table rows being mapped to typed records, so the HTML route still needs conversion. Missing for 10: explicit table-to-row/typed-column output, evidence of schema-based extraction applied to tables, documented database destination loading, and independent hands-on corroboration that no manual cleanup is needed.

support.subject: As a data engineer, I turn extracted tables into typed rows/JSON I can load into a database without manual cleanup

citations.quote: After partitioning, you can have Unstructured generate representations of each detected table in HTML markup format.
It lets you define the target structure up front. Unstructured then extracts values in a consistent JSON format that matches your fields, ready to use in your own applications.
Create a job to extract only the data that you care about from your documents, which Unstructured outputs as JSON object data records in a format that you define.
Unstructured Transform quickly turns any document into structured data that is ready for your apps, databases, vector stores, AI tools, and agents.
